item.title: Hollywood Brown: I don't know if chances will come, I just have to work
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Hollywood Brown was active for the Eagles' Week 1 game against the Commanders, but he never got on the field during the 24-22 win.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Hollywood Brown was active for the Eagles' Week 1 game against the Commanders, but he never got on the field during the 24-22 win.

Brown said this week that there were "no conversations" with coaches leading up to the game about his role. Head coach Nick Sirianni said on Monday that they "obviously want to get him into the football game because his speed is real," but that the rotations "just didn't work out that way" last Sunday.

Brown said he is unsure if anything will change against the Titans this week, but that he'll work to be ready for any opportunity that might come his way.

“That I don’t know,” Brown said, via Ryan Novozinsky of the Philadelphia Inquirer. “I just got to come to work. If it do, it do. If it don’t, it don’t.”

Brown was added to Friday's injury report as a full participant with a hamstring injury, but has no injury designation for Sunday. Whether that means he'll be on the field remains up in the air.

item.title: Mike Sainristil says he'll stay positive after Dan Quinn called his play "not acceptable"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Sainristil's coverage breakdown gave up a touchdown pass against the Eagles, and Quinn called him out afterward.
item.content:encoded:
When discussing the Week 1 loss to the Eagles, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn made a specific point of saying that cornerback Mike Sainristil didn't play well enough. Sainristil says he's staying positive.

Quinn doesn't often call out players by name, but during his Monday press conference after Sunday's loss, he named Sainristil, whose coverage breakdown gave up an Eagles touchdown pass, as one of the players who needed to correct the way he played.

"We’ve definitely identified a few things that, ‘Hey, man, these are the things that we have to get corrected,’" Quinn said.
"Mike’s a very good competitor. I’m certain that we will, but to have that type of play and just not have the right focus at the right time, completely not acceptable.”

Sainristil told reporters in the Commanders' locker room this week that he won't let that get him down.

"People sometimes focus on, What did I do bad? But you don't play a game and do all bad things. You have to focus on the good things, keep the good things good," Sainristil said. "I'm not somebody that sits there, whether I played good, whether I played bad, a few good plays or a few bad plays, I'm not going to sit there sulking."

Sainristil said he'll always try to get better, whether his coach calls him out or not.

"For me, it's just focusing on, What can I do better, every single day?" Sainristil said. "Whether I played good or whether I played bad."

item.title: Potential victims of 49ers imposter Daejon Love now exceed 60
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Daejon Love's scam worked incredibly well.
item.content:encoded:
Daejon Love's scam worked incredibly well. Until it didn't.

Via Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, the FBI has identified 35 more potential victims of the fraud allegedly perpetrated by Love and Taylor Chan. The total number of possible victims now exceeds 60.

"We were surprised how many people were victimized in such a short period of time and then to have that many more come forward," FBI agent Doug Olson said at a news conference, per Kahler. "It's a large volume for just a couple of subjects. Our concern is that this fraud could be replicated by other individuals that are out there victimizing other people in similar schemes."

The FBI believes even more potential victims could be identified.

"We don't want anyone to be fearful of coming forward," Olson said, "certainly not for fear of embarrassment or anything like that, because we want to help them and we want to make sure that this doesn't happen to anybody else."

Love, 35, and Chan, 18, allegedly stole more than $1.3 million, with Love posing as a 49ers player. Chan posed as Love's financial adviser.

"The victims in this case were targeted precisely because they were trusting, responsible people who they believed were building genuine relationships and legitimate financial futures," Olson said. "They were deliberately manipulated through an extremely sophisticated scheme that blended fake personas, fabricated investment accounts, staged video calls and AI-reinforced false identities."

A 49ers source told Kahler that the team was not aware of Love, and that it had not received any reports about him before learning about the situation from the FBI in August.

And while most realize that anything that seems too good to be true probably is, our nature can make us susceptible to getting scammed. Hopefully, the potential victims won't fear ridicule for seeking justice — that alone could cause them and other victims of other scams to say nothing for fear of being embarrassed.

They're the victims. They deserve no scrutiny for being on the wrong side of a criminal enterprise that was very successful. Until, again, it wasn't.

item.title: DeForest Buckner: Colts didn't play up to our standards, whatsoever
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Colts' defense gave up 304 passing yards and 202 rushing yards in their Week 1 loss to the Ravens, and Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner says it was unacceptable.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts' defense gave up 304 passing yards and 202 rushing yards in their Week 1 loss to the Ravens, and Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner says it was unacceptable.

"We didn't play to our standard at all whatsoever, and we know we're better than that and what we put on tape," Buckner said, via JJ Stankevitz of Colts.com. "But obviously, you're only as good as your last game and that's what we put on tape. So we got to continue to prove to ourselves and prove to everybody else that we're a better defense than that."

The Colts are 6.5-point underdogs at Kansas City on Sunday night, and they know they need to play a lot better, or else Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker can put up the same kinds of numbers that Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry did. Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he's emphasizing not letting Walker break tackles.

"The big thing is tackling, right? That's the biggest thing," Steichen said. "You got to get this guy on the ground. He runs low, he runs hard, and then our run fits have got to be great."

If the Colts' defense again doesn't play up to its standards, it could be an ugly night against the Chiefs.

item.title: Jerry Jones: The Giants were better than we thought they were
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Jones seemingly tries to temper expectations for the 2026 Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
The latest Cowboys' season of high expectations started with a thud on Sunday night, when Dallas lost to the Giants in the regular-season opener.

In a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones acknowledged that the outcome had something to do with the opponent.

"They just did a good job all over," Jones said regarding the Giants. "And I will tell you, they were better than we thought they were. I'm anxious to see how New York continues to play, but I really — combination of things. We didn't play as well as we should play and can play, but they played better than I thought they could."

Was it also a product of the Cowboys not being as good as Jones had thought they would be?

"Of course," Jones said. "Well, and to say it that way, I'd rather say it more positively. We're not at the level that we thought we would be.

"I can give you a lot of reasons, logical reasons. We're dealing with a conceptually new coaching staff, dealing with a 'new' to a lot of people out there. The defensive scheme. And then you're dealing with people who are fresh into that scheme. Now, you got some really veteran players out there. But still, they're changing up some of the things that they're doing. Are they capable of doing what we're asking? Absolutely they are.

"But the bottom line is that the last time, frankly, the last time that, from my perspective, that we had as many changes on defense, we had as many changes with the coaching staff, had as much change with the personnel, and had as much change with the team was the first year Jimmy Johnson was our coach, and we won one football game.

"Now, things have changed, and you can come in with less experience than you could in those days. But having said that, it's a challenge now to put it together and get it ready to go. We didn't play well last week. I said — what I meant to say was, New York had really more to do with it than I thought they would. Than I thought they would. And so that's a factor. But Washington could have a lot to do with it here Sunday, too, so we've got to be ready to step up the level of play. There's no question."

It's a sensible explanation. But it cuts against the vibe that had been created before the season, when season tickets were being renewed and hype was being generated and fans were being persuaded that things would be different this year.

What should the real expectations be? With Jerry suggesting that the Cowboys undergone an overhaul they haven't experienced since the year Jones bought the team, they perhaps should be a lot lower than they were a week ago.

item.title: Dolphins DE Chop Robinson in concussion protocol, out for Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Dolphins defensive end Chop Robinson will not play Sunday against the 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
Dolphins defensive end Chop Robinson will not play Sunday against the 49ers.

Robinson was diagnosed with a concussion during Wednesday's practice, and he remains in concussion protocol.

The Dolphins remained out West, practicing in Napa, California, after last week's season opener against the Raiders.

Robinson was limited on Wednesday's injury report and did not practice Thursday.

The Dolphins will lean on Josh Uche, Clelin Ferrell, Rob Beal Jr. and Malik Herring to get after Brock Purdy, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said, via Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.


  • "It’s all of the above. We might do some other things to help out," Hafley said. "But I have confidence in those guys. . . . They've done a good job at practice this week, and it'll be the next man up."

Robinson, drafted 21st overall in 2024, has 10 sacks in his career and had three pressures in Week 1.

Robinson had two concussions in 2025, which kept him sidelined for two games.

Inside linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr. (hamstring) also won't play.

Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder) is questionable after three consecutive limited practices.

item.title: Kirb Herbstreit offers flimsy defense for ESPN's decision to interview Ted Cruz on College GameDay
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: ESPN committed a bizarre broadcasting faux pas last Saturday, by giving Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on College GameDay to push for the passage of the so-called Protect College Sports Act (which also could be called the Screw College Players Act or, as Simms suggested, Protect the ESPN and SEC Contract Act).
item.content:encoded:
ESPN committed a bizarre broadcasting faux pas last Saturday, by giving Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on College GameDay to push for the passage of the so-called Protect College Sports Act (which also could be called the Screw College Players Act or, as Simms suggested, Protect the ESPN and SEC Contract Act). The story has resonated throughout the week, and it looms over Saturday's episode of College GameDay in Oxford, Mississippi.

Kirk Herbstreit, one of the College GameDay analysts, addressed the situation in comments with reporters on Friday.

"I was first really impressed," Herbstreit said, via Mississippi Today. "I've never seen a guy booed that long and be able to just power through that. You know, I don't know if he could hear what I could hear, but it was pretty — I think he was booed pretty much the entire time he spoke.

"I don't really get into politics. It's just not — I'm kind of an independent guy, right down the middle of the fairway. I'm for America, so whoever helps us as a country, I'm for. Whether it's somebody on the left, somebody on the right, so I don't really follow it. I don't know anything about his political views. I don't know what he's for or against. I care about football, my family, and my faith, and my country. Those are things I love.

"And so, I don't really pick sides, and I was surprised. I didn't know what his deal was, so him being booed, I asked people, 'Like, what's going on here?' And we had him on because they were gonna be voting this week, and maybe he could give us some insight to what's going on. That was really it. So we're not picking sides in any way at all. We just want to see the chaos that's surrounding this sport kind of be reeled in, and if this will help us get to that, then great. Now, the fact that the guy that sits right next to me, Nick Saban, was heavily involved in putting this act together, this guy loves college football more than anybody I've ever met. And so if he's happy about what this could do, then I follow his lead. But yeah, that was surprising. But, again, I don't really follow it, so I didn't really understand it."

There's a lot to unpack there. I'll keep it simple. Herbstreit is either flat-out lying or he's ridiculously naive.

How can anyone say "I love my country" while being completely detached from the issues that shape its present and future? How can any American adult not know what it means to be a Republican or to be a Democrat, and how those labels have become so inherently polarizing and conducive to negative reactions?

Beyond Herbstreit's claim that he's clueless as to why someone like Ted Cruz would be booed, Herbstreit's position that he's "right down the middle of the fairway" and that ESPN isn't "picking sides" on the issue at hand can't be reconciled with his viewpoint that the "chaos" needs to "kind of be reeled in" and that he supports anything Nick Saban recommends on the matter because Saban "loves college football more than anybody I've met."

It's entirely possible to love college football and to want to limit player pay and mobility. Which is precisely what the Screw College Players Act will do.

The word "chaos" is a matter of perspective. From the players' perspective, it's not chaotic; they have real rights and power. From the perspective of those who don't like the fact that the rabbit has the gun, it's definitely chaotic. Because the rabbit has the gun.

The best news is that folks seem to be figuring out what's going on here. The powers-that-be don't like the fact that they've lost some of their power, given the implosion of a system that was fueled by antitrust violations that collectively prevented players from getting paid. In the aftermath of the reckoning, those who don't like the new reality are shedding crocodile tears and screaming "the sky is falling" to anyone who may be able to help them implement a system that limits the new rights the players enjoy.

It's a grift. It's a scam. Herbstreit has made himself part of that scam while pretending to be neutral — and not even his dog will shield him from the criticism he now deserves.

item.title: Azeez Al-Shaair on publicizing Hind Rajab's story: Most of you might not even know who she was
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for writing the name "Hind Rajab" on his eye-black strips during a Week 1 game against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for writing the name "Hind Rajab" on his eye-black strips during a Week 1 game against the Bills. On Friday, Al-Shaair explained his decision to publicize the name of the five-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed, along with six family members, by Israeli forces in 2024.

"I think everybody knows what it's about," Al-Shaair said, via D.J. Bien-Aime of ESPN. "I think that was the point. Because before that, probably most of you guys might not even know who she was. That's kind of the point.

"There a lot that goes on in the world, not just overseas, right here in our own country. . . . This past Tuesday, a friend of mine, literally just sitting there crying in front of me on the phone, come to find out her cousin, who's been here since he was five years old, got detained on the way to a concert and is being deported. Mind you, he has no family, no nothing over there. And that was my first interaction, my first experience, with somebody that I personally know. . . .

"There's a lot of issues that I speak on, that's really just to shed a light, because a lot of people don't care nothing about it. . . . We're blessed to be able to have the comforts of, you know, living in the United States and not having to worry about certain things, but there's issues here and all over the world that, you know, when you talk about even what happened with Hind Rajab and her family, those are taxpaying dollars that we're — as Americans — are paying, that are being used to bomb innocent men, women, and children. So that's really what that was about."

Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving offered to pay the fine. Al-Shaair said that he and Irving "align on the cause, which is humanity; we both care about humanity."

"Regardless of skin color, race, anything like that," Al-Shaair said. "That's what I think, more than anything, when it comes to me and him, that we align on, and just not being afraid to do that. . . . We don't have to have all the answers to everything to know that an innocent man, an innocent woman, an innocent child losing their life is not right. Like, I don't need anybody to gaslight me into saying that, 'Well, you gotta ask. . . .' I just know that's not right, whether they're here in America or somewhere halfway across the world."

It remains to be seen whether Al-Shaair will have a similar message during Sunday's game against the Bengals, and whether the league will threaten to keep him from playing if he does.

Nacua missed practice with a hip injury. It is unclear whether it is related to the psoas soreness that forced him to leave the joint practice with the Cowboys early on Aug. 13. The psoas is a deep core muscle and a primary hip flexor.

Nacua was not listed on the injury report for Week 1.

Nacua’s backup, Jordan Whittington, also missed Friday's practice. Whittington has a quad injury.

Safety Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) was the other player who didn't practice.

Safety Kam Curl (ankle), inside linebacker Omar Speights (hip) and inside linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder) were limited.

Wide receiver Davante Adams returned to practice Friday after a rest day on Thursday.

item.title: Aaron Donald plans to play on Monday night
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The return of the three-time Defensive Player of the Year will come against the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Donald is ready to return.

Donald, the Rams defensive tackle who hasn't played since announcing his retirement after the 2023 season, said today that he expects to play against the Giants on Monday Night Football.

"That's the plan," Donald said when asked if he is playing.

Donald, who did not make the trip to Australia for the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers, said he has been feeling like his old self while practicing this week.

"Have another practice tomorrow, and then we'll see, but feeling good," Donald said.

The 35-year-old Donald was the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 2017, 2018 and 2020. He retired after 10 seasons with the Rams but started considering a comeback after the Rams traded for the NFL's reigning Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett.

Donald and Garrett on the same defensive line would be a ferocious combination, but we'll have to wait at least four more weeks to see that, as Garrett went on injured reserve after Week 1. Instead, the focus on Monday night will be on Donald, and seeing whether he still looks like the Aaron Donald of old.

item.title: Deshaun Watson could lose seventh straight start on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's been a long week for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a long week for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. And it's still not over.

Against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Watson could post his seventh straight loss as a starter. That would be the longest streak for any Browns quarterback since DeShone Kizer in 2017, when a 15-game losing streak cemented an 0-16 season. Which opened the door to drafting Baker Mayfield the following April.

Watson drew fresh criticism after the Week 1 34-10 loss to the Jaguars by claiming that the "media has this expectation that I’m supposed to throw [for] 400 yards and five touchdowns every week," even though he hasn't done that once since Week 5 of the 2019 season.

There are even more depressing statistics than that. As Anthony Lima of 92.3 The Fan observed on Friday morning, Bills quarterback Josh Allen has nine total touchdowns in five days. Watson has eight total touchdowns in 1,041 days.

And, yes, the Browns could have drafted Allen instead of Mayfield. But don't feel too bad about that, Browns fans; the organization likely would have ruined and/or moved on from Allen by now, too.

After Sunday — barring a win and, perhaps, 400 yards and five touchdowns — the Browns will have to move on from Watson or risk a full-blown riot for the Week 3 home opener against Carolina.

item.title: Report: Steelers have received no serious trade inquiries about Joey Porter Jr.
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the contract impasse lingers between the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., none of the other 31 teams has made a move to try to get him.
item.content:encoded:
As the contract impasse lingers between the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., none of the other 31 teams has made a move to try to get him.

A lengthy article from ESPN exploring the dynamics of the situation contains this key line: "[T]he team has neither made nor received any serious inquiries about the cornerback."

Given that it's been obvious for weeks that Porter and the Steelers aren't seeing eye-to-eye on a potential extension, interested teams have had every reason to spark a dialogue. The absence of any such effort suggests that no one is willing to pay Porter what he wants and to give the Steelers what they'd need.

ESPN also points to two primary issues with the negotiations. One, the two sides have a "significant difference" about Porter's value. Two, Porter wants the team to break from its habit of fully guaranteeing compensation beyond the first year of the contract.

The Steelers historically had done that only for high-end quarterbacks, like Ben Roethlisberger. As noted by ESPN, they broke from that precedent with linebacker T.J. Watt, twice.

As not noted by ESPN, they also deviated from this habit when trading for, and signing, receiver DK Metcalf in 2025; he got $60 million fully guaranteed over the first two years.

While cash-flow concerns possibly will keep the Steelers from expanding the practice to a player who won't be paid at the top of the market, the bigger issue seems to be the value of the contract.

Either way, the team's other internal rule regarding not doing new deals after the season begins has put everyone in an awkward spot. As noted by Steelers Depot, the team made an exception in 1995 for safety Darren Perry. At the time, the explanation from Ed Bouchette of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette was that "if they were close to a deal that would carry it over to the early part of the season."

In this case, they could try something like "we'll do a deal before the first game of the season in which the player plays."

Semantics don't matter, since no deal is close. And it's possible Porter will continue to not play until the Steelers trade him for whatever they can get.

As an unnamed "source with knowledge of the situation" told ESPN, "I don't know if he ever puts on a Steelers uniform again."

For now, he won't put on a uniform for the second game of the 2026 season. With no end to the standoff in sight, it could continue on a weekly basis until he's traded or the Steelers decide to play hardball by fining him for refusing to play.

item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks ruled quarterback Sam Darnold out for Week 2 a couple of days ago, but his health was still a topic for head coach Mike Macdonald during Friday's press conference.

Darnold has not practiced since injuring his glute in the team's season-opening win over the Patriots and Macdonald didn't provide much sense about when that would change.

“He’s on his way back," Macdonald said. "Is it next week? Is it the week after, the week after that? I’m not sure. I’m optimistic, put it that way.”

Drew Lock will start against the Cardinals with Jalen Milroe serving as their backup.

Safety Ty Okada (hamstring) will also mean the game. Safety Nick Emmanwori (hip, ankle) and guard Anthony Bradford (knee, hip) are both listed as questionable.

item.title: Joe Brady: If DJ Moore can be out there for Week 3, he’ll be out there
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After defeating the Lions on Thursday night, the Bills will have a long weekend to rest up and heal before hosting the Chargers in Week 3.
item.content:encoded:
After defeating the Lions on Thursday night, the Bills will have a long weekend to rest up and heal before hosting the Chargers in Week 3.

That's good news for a club that has a pair of key players banged up.

Head coach Joe Brady did not have much of an update on receiver DJ Moore — who exited the game with a shoulder injury — or Ed Oliver, who was inactive after injuring his hip during pregame warm-ups.

"We’re still obviously going through [it]," Brady said. "One of the perks of the Thursday night game, not a lot of perks, but one of the perks of it is you do get that long weekend, and guys will recover. So we don’t practice again until next Wednesday. No different than any other — we’ll see how these guys are going to recover and how their body will take it. As you guys who have been around DJ or know DJ’s past, he’s as tough as they come. So, if he can be out there, he’ll be out there.

"[Oliver is] another guy, we’ll just see how he’s progressing," Brady added. "The guys that are getting tests and MRIs and all that, they’re getting that now."

Additionally, Brady noted that running back Ty Johnson and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders were close to playing against the Lions. With the extended break before Week 3, both may be able to be back for Buffalo’s next game.

The Bills will host the Chargers on Sunday, Sept. 27.

item.title: Bills are third team ever to start 2-0 while giving up more than 30 points in both games
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Bills have started the season with two wins over two teams that entered the season as favorites to win their divisions.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills have started the season with two wins over two teams that entered the season as favorites to win their divisions. They have to be pleased with their 36-31 win over the Texans and their 41-31 win over the Lions.

At least, they have to be pleased with scoring 36 and 41 points in their first two games. Giving up 31 points in each game is not so pleasing.

In fact, the Bills are just the third team ever to start the season 2-0 despite giving up more than 30 points in both games. Previously, the 2000 Rams won their first two games by scores of 41-36 and 37-34, and the 1991 Bills won their first two games 35-31 and 52-34.

Via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press, only four teams in NFL history have given up 62 or more points while starting 2-0: This year's Bills, those 2000 Rams and 1991 Bills, and the 2018 Chiefs.

The good news for the Bills is, the three previous teams to give up 62 or more points while starting 2-0 made the playoffs. The bad news is, all three of them lost in the postseason — and all three of them gave up more than 30 points in those losses.

The Bills' offense looks great through two weeks of the season. It remains to be seen whether they can win a championship with this defense.
